public_rationale: OpenAI acknowledged remaining hallucinations at launch. The original Sparks paper also documented a failed multistep plan. Together these establish that factual reliability and planning remained unsolved in the ordinary sense Marcus used. They do not imply that GPT-4 failed every planning task or had made no progress.
limitations: The planning example concerns the early research model examined in Sparks.
These items establish persistent failures, not their frequency across all uses.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-4 has not solved hallucinations, reliability, or planning on complex tasks.

statement.excerpt: The problem of hallucinations is not solved; reliability is not solved; planning on complex tasks is (as the authors themselves acknowledge) not solved.
statement.document_title: The Sparks of AGI? Or the End of Science?

our_interpretation: Read as saying material factual, reasoning, and multistep-planning failures remained, rather than denying improvements.
Hallucinations and invalid plans are evidence of unreliability; these are overlapping assertions.
Use the March 2023 launch-period findings available before March 24, including the early model studied in Sparks.
criteria.support_condition: Documented hallucinations and planning failures show that GPT-4 remained materially unreliable in these areas.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that the contemporaneous model had overcome the identified factual and planning failure modes across suitably varied tests.
